title: The finite affine Cech model transported from the canonical base chart
statement: Let $f:X\to T$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-morphism-conventions], $F$ an $\mathcal O_X$-module, and $V:\operatorname{Fin}(r)\to X.\mathrm{Opens}$ a finite family. Form the specified complex [def-pc-affine-alternating-cech-model] for $f$ composed with $T\to\operatorname{Spec}\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$, then pull it back termwise to $T$. This is the definition of $C(f,F,V)$, with no choice of a witness. Its terms are quasi-coherent, its negative terms are zero, and its terms in degrees greater than $r$ are zero. No affineness, covering, flatness or cohomology claim is required for these three properties.

proof.text: Use the existing affine alternating section complex, restricting scalars along the composite to the spectrum of the base global ring, associating sheaves, then applying pullback along the canonical base chart. All data are actual functor constructions.

Extension by embeddingUpNat gives zero negative terms, preserved by the additive functors. In degree n greater than r, an order embedding Fin(n+1) into Fin(r) would contradict Fintype.card_le_of_injective. The increasing-tuple product is therefore over an empty index type, hence a zero module. Map this zero object through scalar restriction, tilde and pullback. Tilde terms are quasi-coherent and pullback preserves quasi-coherence.
